name: renodx
readmeExcerpt:
# renodx
RenoDX, short for "Renovation Engine for DirectX Games", is a toolset to mod games. Currently it can replace shaders, inject buffers, add overlays, upgrade swapchains, upgrade texture resources, and write user settings to disk. Because RenoDX uses Reshade's add-on system, compatibility is expected to be pretty wide. Using Reshade simplifies all the hooks necessary to tap into DirectX without worrying about patching version-specific exe files.


# Contributing

* See [CONTRIBUTING.md](./docs/CONTRIBUTING.md)
* For the live devkit and MCP workflow, see [DEVKIT_MCP.md](./docs/DEVKIT_MCP.md)

# Mods

* See [Mods page](https://github.com/clshortfuse/renodx/wiki/Mods)

# Utilities

* [renodx-fpslimiter.addon64](https://clshortfuse.github.io/renodx/renodx-fpslimiter.addon64) – FPS Limiter
* [renodx-devkit.addon64](https://clshortfuse.github.io/renodx/renodx-devkit.addon64) – Developer kit to help build addons
* [decomp.exe](https://clshortfuse.github.io/renodx/decomp.exe) – Shader Model 6.0+ Decompiler

aiSummary.oneLiner: A universal DirectX modding toolset built on Reshade to upgrade shaders, inject buffers, and manage game assets.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: RenoDX provides a unified renovation engine for modifying DirectX games without requiring game-specific executable patches. It solves the complexity of graphics modding by leveraging Reshade's add-on system to establish deep, universal hooks into the DirectX rendering pipeline. The engine allows developers to intercept and replace shaders, upgrade texture resources, and inject custom buffers on the fly. It also includes capabilities for modifying swapchains to enable modern display features like HDR. By abstracting the low-level API calls, RenoDX establishes a standardized framework for creating highly compatible visual mods.
keyFeatures: Shader replacement: Intercepts and replaces original game shaders dynamically during rendering.
Reshade integration: Utilizes Reshade's add-on architecture for broad compatibility across DirectX titles.
Buffer injection: Allows developers to inject custom data buffers into the rendering pipeline.
Swapchain upgrades: Modifies DirectX swapchains to support advanced display technologies like HDR.
Asset management: Upgrades texture resources dynamically without permanently altering game files.

useCases.title: HDR retrofitting
useCases.description: Add native High Dynamic Range support to older DirectX games that were originally mastered in SDR.

useCases.title: Visual remastering
useCases.description: Replace low-resolution textures and outdated shaders with modern equivalents across an entire game engine.

useCases.title: Custom overlays
useCases.description: Inject diagnostic overlays or new UI elements directly into the DirectX rendering pipeline.

useCases.title: Universal modding
useCases.description: Develop graphics mods that function across multiple games sharing similar DirectX API calls without reverse-engineering executables.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Technical artists, graphics programmers, and modders looking to significantly alter the visual output of DirectX games. It requires an understanding of graphics pipelines, shaders, and Reshade architecture.
